messages:
Alex Chen: getting multiple customer reports — hosted inference returning 503s around 12:40 UTC. spike started ~12:37 :eyes:
oncall-bot: ALERT: hosted-infer-gateway p95 503s > 5% for 3m (clusters: pool-a). see https://status.internal/infer/alerts/1718501234
Alex Chen: digging into logs now, but early signs of worker crashes (segfault) during hotmodel swap. stack shows nvml/gpu mem allocation failures + SIGSEGV
Maria Singh: which model and which pool? any env changes rolled recently?
Alex Chen: model: rdx-large-quant-v2, pool: hosted-gpu-pool-a, roll started at 12:35 for canary. no infra changes scheduled.
Chao Li: fyi I saw a few OOM-kernel messages in dmesg earlier on node-gpu-17, might be fragmentation rather than raw alloc size.
Samir Patel: can we confirm if spike correlates with large-context/longstream requests? those keep KV cache and increase working set.
Alex Chen: correlating now — customer A and B sent long contexts (~100k tokens total). stacktrace snippet:
```
signal 11 (SIGSEGV), code 1 (SEGV_MAPERR) at 0x7f2a3b1c
Backtrace: infer_runner+0x1a3b4
NVML: failed to allocate 0x3f00000, ret=9
```
Chao Li: NVML ret=9 is out-of-memory on driver side. fragmentation + persistent KV cache growth could hit it.
Maria Singh: are these requests routed to dedicated slots or shared-hosted?
Alex Chen: shared-hosted. routing was trying to spin up new replica during canary and that worker crashed on first init. subsequent retries caused 503s.
Support Bot: Escalation ticket created: #ESCL-2026-4887. Notifying CS.
Samir Patel: mitigation idea: rollback canary to previous quantized artifact or force model restart policy to avoid prefetch at init (disable prefetch).
Chao Li: quick mitigation: mark pool-a as draining for hotmodel-swap, fall back to pool-b. I'll add routing rule to avoid spinning new replicas in pool-a.
Alex Chen: doing drain now: `curl -XPOST -H \"Authorization: Bearer $OPS_TOKEN\" https://api.internal/pools/pool-a/drain`
Maria Singh: also bumping auto-retry throttles to prevent cascade.
Alex Chen: drain submitted. switching traffic to pool-b in 1m.
oncall-bot: ACTION: routing-rule updated, pool-a weight=0, pool-b weight=100 (by Maria Singh)
Samir Patel: longer term: we should add a pre-init mem-check to avoid starting quantized model on nodes with fragmented free blocks. file a ticket for runtime check.
Chao Li: creating repro job to simulate large KV prefetch + model swap. will run on staging (node-gpu-stg-9) and attach heap/dmesg.
Alex Chen: CS oncall pinged customers, telling them we routed around and mitigation in flight.
Support Bot: Customer update posted to #support-incidents and ticket ESCL-2026-4887 updated.
Maria Singh: next steps: 1) repro on staging 2) add pre-init mem guard 3) revert canary or change init strategy 4) longer-term kernel/allocator tuning. I'll own rollout coordination.
Samir Patel: also add a temporary guard in router: if canary init fails >2x within 5m, stop canary and revert automatically. reduces blast radius.
Alex Chen: noted. for postmortem collect: node dmesg, infer logs, model artifact, exact request payloads (CS ok to share redacted).
Chao Li: running repro now, will paste logs when complete.
Alex Chen: thanks all — 503s down to normal after routing change. keeping thread open until staging repro confirms root cause. :thumbsup:
